newsitem.title: THAILAND: PRESS DIGEST - Thai newspapers - March 13.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Thai newspapers - March 13.

text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Thai press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- The Criminal Court deputy chief justice who granted bail to a suspected heroin trafficker wanted by Washington will be removed temporarily from the bench to facilitate an investigation. If corruption was found to be a factor in the decision, Somchai Udomwong would face criminal and disciplinary action. Somchai released Li Yun Chung, or Pongsak Rojanasaksakul, on five-million-baht bail, for 30 days on February 7. (BANGKOK POST, THE NATION)

- The Thai-Burma Friendship Bridge will open in two months, the army commander says. Work on the final stage of the project, which was 95 percent complete before it was suspended almost two years ago, started last week. (BANGKOK POST)

- Two House committees and the Social Action Party have decried the impact of the massive national budget cuts on rural projects, and the rumblings of discontent threatened to escalate into a political earthquake for Finance Minister Amnuay Viravan. Both government and opposition members of parliament have been upset by the drastic reduction in funding for the construction of rural roads and Amnuay, the key architect of the 106 billion baht cut, can expect few sympathisers if he faces parliamentary scrutiny on the matter. (THE NATION)

- Thai Danu Bank and Finance One take their first official steps towards merging tomorrow when they sign a memorandum of understanding at the Bank of Thailand (BOT). A high level source at Thai Danu Bank says the official contract-signing ceremony has already been arranged at the BOT through central bank Governor Rerngchai Marakanond, who will also be a witness. (BUSINESS DAY)

- Industry Minister Korn Dabaransi begins a two-day visit to Burma today, during which he will discuss with the Petroleum Authority of Thailand (PTT) the possibility of reducing the price of natural gas. Korn is scheduled to sign a contract with the Burmese government to purchase natural gas from Burma's Yetagun gas field. (BUSINESS DAY)

- The government has agreed in principle to allow foreigners to purchase 100 percent of condominium projects in an effort to reduce the property oversupply. It has also agreed to tax incentives to encourage interest. (THE NATION)
